page: Microsoft Azure M176bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 176 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 88 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 1536.0 GB of RAM, providing 8.73 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable and designed for block storage performance.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and PassMark CPU score all rank in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also place in the top 10%, though the PassMark memory score is in the middle 50%. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the middle 50%, while Geekbench single-core and image processing rank in the top 25%. The CPU supports Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which contribute to top-tier scores in extended instructions and encryption tests.

With high memory density and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this server is designed for memory-intensive and compute-heavy workloads. It achieves top-tier performance in PassMark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput. It also demonstrates strong performance in LLM inference for 7B and 70B models. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external block storage, which represents an architectural tradeoff. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of dedicated Intel Xeon cores and massive memory capacity make it suitable for large-scale databases, enterprise applications, and memory-bound simulation tasks without the overhead of a GPU.
